name: right: at once
note: "Seek medical help right away", "see your doctor right away": the word where it means at once. It also fires on "right now" and "right up to", a little less; the next latent fires most on "right now".

name: right: this moment
note: "Your body is going through tremendous changes right now". It also answers, more weakly, to "right for you" and to "right-click": the senses of the written word are not fully apart.

name: order: In order to, opening a sentence
note: "In order to consider this question, ...": the phrase at the head of a sentence. In mid-sentence the same phrase belongs to the next latent.

name: order: in order to, in mid-sentence
note: "... from huge amounts of Internet data in order to learn more": the same phrase after the main clause, with "in addition" and "in an attempt" as rarer company.

name: order: an arrangement, a command
note: "The order of the different prayers", "first-order neurons", "Order for home delivery today!", "ordered by Air Combat Command".

name: case: a case study
note: "A Case Study in ...", and the name "Case Western"; more weakly the phrase "in the case of".

name: case: an instance of a disease
note: "Reports a case of smallpox", "newly diagnosed TB cases": the case a doctor counts. It also fires on "instances" and "patients".

name: case: in case
note: "In case you haven't been following": the conjunction. "In the event of" fires it too, more weakly.

name: back: back in time
note: "Traceable back to the earliest of human ...", "going back as far as": its direction raises "generations", "decades", "centuries".

name: back: returning
note: "Settle back to their normal states", "pumped back through our taps": back to where something was.

name: like: similar to
note: "Like their B-cell counterparts, ...", "Like many such states, ...": the comparison that opens a sentence, and "Unlike".

name: like: looks like, feels like
note: "It feels like a fresh start", "It looks like you're using ...": after a verb of seeming. "Resembles" fires it too.

name: Hebrew letters
note: Text in the Hebrew alphabet, letter by letter: a script has a latent of its own, though nearly everything the model read was English.

name: inside a web address
note: The pieces of a domain name between "www." and ".com": its direction raises ".org", ".com", ".net", ".edu".

name: the end of a table row
note: The bar and line break that close a row of a table written with bars; its direction raises the bar that opens the next row.

name: THE, in capitals
note: "THE SATURDAY EVENING ...": the article in capital letters at the head of a title.

name: an adverb that comments on the sentence
note: "But, interestingly, ...", "But strangely, ...": the ending -ly of a word that judges what the sentence goes on to say.

name: founded, created, established
note: "Founded in 2009 by", "Founded in 1824": the verb that brings an institution into being, strongest at the head of a sentence about it; "formed" and "launched" fire it too.

name: to understand, recognize, remember that
note: "It is important to understand that ...", "First, recognize what ...": a verb of knowing that waits for its clause; its direction raises "that", "why", "how".

name: food
note: "Beef, pork and lamb", "spinach", "lettuce", "pasta": the names of foods, piece by piece, wherever they are spelled.

name: God, by any name
note: Strongest on "Hashem", then "God", "Lord", "Christ", and "He" with a capital: the one referred to, not one word for him.

name: medicine: who gives care
note: "Paramedics must be calm, cool", "primary care", "one doctor actually said to a patient": physicians, doctors, care, patients.

name: electronics
note: "Resistor", "MOSFET", "capacitance", "cathode", "antennas": the parts and quantities of a circuit.

name: reading a genome
note: "Open reading frames", "sequence changes", "complete genome sequence analysis": it stays on through a passage about DNA sequences, token after token.

name: pigs and pork
note: "Fetal pig dissection", "swine influenza", "pork", and also the first piece of "pigmentation": the latent follows the letters as well as the animal.

name: the tropics
note: "Fragile tropical fish", "neglected tropical diseases", "temperate climates", "the equator": zones of climate.

name: a plant's botanical name
note: "Camellia sinensis (L.) O. Kuntze", "the Leguminosae family", "a member of the ginger family": Latin names and families of plants.

name: a passage about language
note: "English is the official language of ...", "North Indian languages including ...": weak and steady on most tokens of a passage about languages; its direction raises "languages" and "dialects".

name: the byline
note: "by William Fryer", "By Janice Harayda": the word by that opens a line naming an author.

name: Posted, at the head of a post
note: "Posted August 17th", "Posted by KatNip on": the first word of a blog post's date line; "Filed under" fires it too.

name: the day that opens a dateline
note: "Monday January 18", "Tuesday, August 29": a weekday or a month at the start of a line.

name: the last full stop of a page
note: "Comments are closed.", "... published in the journal PRX Quantum.": the period after which the document ends; its direction raises the document-start mark and "Copyright".

name: Definition, as a heading
note: "Definition of geognosy": the word that opens a dictionary entry, with "Description" and "Summary".

name: a list is about to begin
note: "You may either:", "We want all children to:": the colon before a list; its direction raises the bullet.

name: inside a citation
note: "(Hoffmann et al. ...", "(Simons and Ambinder, ...": on the authors' names and through the citation; its direction raises "et" and "doi".

name: attention comes next
note: "Pay particular attention", "Pay close attention": on the adjective after "pay"; its direction raises "attention", "consideration", "heed".

name: a university comes next
note: "Professor of history at the University of Iowa": on "at" after a post; its direction raises "University", "Harvard", "MIT".

name: risk comes next
note: "People with a family history of leukemia are also at higher risk": on the words before a risk is named; its direction raises "risk", "odds", "likelihood", "chances".

name: type 2 diabetes comes next
note: "A risk factor for type 2 diabetes": on "type", before the number is written; its direction raises the second piece of "diabetes".

name: of comes next
note: "Under the guidance of", "at the behest of", "under the charge of": a noun that takes of; its direction raises "of".

name: and comes next
note: "Mining and Materials", "Greenberg and Baron": the first of two names; its direction raises "and" and the ampersand.

name: than comes next
note: "More states are now requiring ...", "a more sustainable operation": on the word after "more"; its direction raises "than".

name: In addition, In fact, In contrast
note: The word In at the head of a sentence, whatever follows it; its direction raises "addition", "fact", "contrast", "conclusion": the continuations it prepares.

name: The reason, The aim, The goal
note: The article The at the head of a sentence, whatever follows it; its direction raises "reason", "aim", "goal", "purpose".

name: right, left, wrong: a side or a verdict
note: "Right ascension", "(Right)" in a caption, "left hand aisle", but also "the right filter medium" and "wrong": the side and the correct choice share one latent.

name: back: a body's back, and other backs
note: "Back pain" and "a brownish back", but also "back-to-school night", "cut back to the main branch" and "front": one latent for several things the word does.
